project.name: Bench Tool Loans — synthetic learning MVP

intention.statement: Prepare a small B2B business experiment for independent electronics repair shops, with a local learning MVP and no build yet.
intention.advice: Test recording friction and current workaround before assuming a business.

user.text: Independent electronics repair shop manager responsible for lending individually identifiable bench tools.

problem.text: Shop managers lose track of who has a loaned bench tool and when it should return.

trigger.text: A bench tool is loaned or someone asks who has it.

job.text: Record custody and due date, find outstanding loans and close returns.

pain.text: Unclear custody of loaned tools; severity and urgency are unverified.

reason_for_belief.text: Synthetic reports and two fitting colleague sessions make a bounded learning test feasible, not commercially validated.

sources.title: Synthetic founder scenario
sources.retainedText: Founder requests local tool-loan learning MVP with borrower, due date, return and outstanding list. Three shop-manager reports are supplied synthetic context. Two fitting colleagues available tomorrow. No build yet; no accounts, payments, messaging, deployment or real customer data.
sources.limitation: Deterministic replay fixture; not current market or customer evidence. Synthetic scenario assertions; no independently verified demand, interviews, observations or permission.

sources.title: Snipe-IT overview
sources.retainedText: Documentation describes uniquely tagged assets checked out to people and checked back in; prevents double-booking.
sources.limitation: Deterministic replay fixture; not current market or customer evidence. Vendor documentation establishes capability, not repair-shop adoption or demand.

sources.title: Snipe-IT pricing
sources.retainedText: Self-hosted software is free; basic hosting publicly lists USD 39.99 billed monthly or USD 399.99 billed annually.
sources.limitation: Deterministic replay fixture; not current market or customer evidence. Public listing checked October 6, 2026; not purchased; self-hosting carries setup and maintenance effort.

sources.title: RepairShopr electronics repair

sources.title: MDN localStorage
sources.retainedText: Browser localStorage persists across sessions for an origin. Direct file URL behavior is undefined; browser policy may block persistence; private-session storage is cleared when private tabs close.
sources.limitation: Deterministic replay fixture; not current market or customer evidence. Documentation, not a runtime test of the proposed MVP.

technical.summary: Feasible in principle as a loopback-served native-browser app; no external dependencies or AI required. No code or runtime evidence yet.
technical.centralRisk: False persistence confidence and failure to log loans in everyday work.

coverage.reason: Manual fictional tool, borrower alias and date only; no external API or imports.
Validate trimmed required fields and calendar date; unique tool label per physical tool; reject second active loan. Actual runtime behavior must be tested.
No third-party service, dataset or library required; choose native browser APIs.
No paid API, hosting or service; local computation only. Build labour not estimated.
Excluded from exact local learning scope.
Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript with a loopback-only static server is a provisional low-complexity approach; no measured latency or implementation yet.
Deterministic record-state transitions; no AI needed.
Use stable HTTP loopback origin, test read/write failures and corrupt stored data. Never display saved/returned until persistence succeeds. Check refresh and restart.
Fictional borrower aliases; loopback binding, no remote assets, telemetry or credentials; render input as text. Everyone with browser-profile access can see records.
Paper/spreadsheet provides a rehearsal control; Snipe-IT offers broader existing checkout. Tiny local prototype is justified only for this bounded workflow test.

options.name: Paper or spreadsheet rehearsal
options.approach: Use tool/borrower/due/returned columns as a control immediately.
options.tradeoff: Tests conceptual workflow without software usability or persistence.

options.name: Tiny local browser prototype
options.approach: One workstation, stable loopback HTTP origin, native browser storage, no remote requests.
options.tradeoff: No sync or backup; explicit storage error handling required.

options.name: Existing Snipe-IT
options.tradeoff: Broader setup and administration than tomorrow's three-task test; no installation authorized.

recommendation.reason: Smallest complete proposed software flow for the requested observation; compare with their current method and stop if unnecessary.

founderFit.edge: Synthetic founder reports access to two fitting colleagues tomorrow.
founderFit.limitation: Access and relationship do not establish independent demand or customer willingness to pay.

learning.reason: Can the log fit the lending moment and outperform the current method? Pain frequency, severity and payment remain unknown.

experiment.promise: On one local workstation, record who has an individually identified bench tool and when it is due, then find and close that loan without coaching.
capabilities: Record a tool loan with unique tool label, borrower alias and due date.
Mark a selected outstanding loan returned.
See outstanding loans with tool, borrower and due date, earliest due first.
cuts: No deployment, cloud sync or shared-device use.
No barcode scanning, inventory integration or analytics.
experiment.limitations: Single browser profile and one active tab; fictional data only. Storage may be cleared or blocked, no backup or sync. Friendly-colleague bias; two sessions test usability and workflow fit, not adoption, fewer losses, retention or demand. No product has been built or tested.
experiment.success: Both fitting colleagues independently create, find and return the correct fictional loan; record time and all hesitation. No false saves, duplicate active tool loans or lost records after reload. Capture concrete past behavior and compare with their current method.
experiment.failure: Either cannot complete the core flow without help, misidentifies a borrower, sees a false save or loses persisted data. If both prefer their current method or report little practical need, pause expansion and investigate pain rather than add features.
